name: Archal

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Simulated API environments, not established arbitrary Linux execution. $0.10 per environment-minute, second prorated; a sandbox with several environments pays each. $5 signup+$15 first ready sandbox. Paid continuation explicitly not available while safety rollout disabled; cannot sustain benchmark from $20 trial.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Concurrency: 'workspace policy limits concurrent sandboxes' (number unpublished); '429 can include Retry-After'; 'capacity can reject new work even when a balance is positive'. Configurable provider-call ceiling 100,000 per sandbox. TTL/idle/hard-expiry per lease; no plan-wide max published.
Product is a catalog of 22 stateful simulated SaaS APIs (GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Supabase, Jira, ...), 110 curated starting states; not a Linux VM/container sandbox. Keep 'alt'.

fleet.verification: Verified signup; homepage explicitly says no card required for introductory usage credits.
fleet.notes: Service/API simulation sandboxes, not a published general VM fleet entitlement. No new-account concurrent sandbox quota or documented increase procedure located.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Billing stops after durable teardown intent, expiry, or a policy stop. Physical runtime deletion can complete afterward.
snapshot_auto.note: Not a machine product. Sandboxes (simulated SaaS API environments) are torn down on TTL/idle/hard expiry; nothing documents saving state automatically on expiry. Diff uses a caller-held 'before', 'not with a hidden snapshot'.

harness_api.quote: Keep Braintrust, LangSmith, custom graders, traces, and test runners in place. Archal provides stateful provider environments. Your coding agent connects those environments to the harness you already trust.
harness_api.note: Section titled 'Archal does not own the harness'; intro: 'Archal does not replace your agent harness, model, evaluator, observability tool, or CI system.' Agent runs outside Archal; setup is via a pasted prompt + 5 repo-local skills for Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/Devin, plus a hosted lifecycle MCP (https://archal.ai/api/mcp) - not a harness-driving API.

egress_allowlist.quote: A stateful environment represents one external service inside the sandbox. It keeps data across requests and exposes provider-shaped REST, MCP, or both.
egress_allowlist.note: Not applicable: no customer code runs inside an Archal sandbox (OpenAPI has no exec/shell/network endpoints), so there is no outbound traffic to control.

egress_http_rules.quote: A stateful environment represents one external service inside the sandbox. It keeps data across requests and exposes provider-shaped REST, MCP, or both.
egress_http_rules.note: Not applicable (no customer code executes in the sandbox). Only a 'configurable provider-call ceiling per sandbox' of 100,000 and request rate limits exist.

ingress_rules.quote: Each ready environment receives a different short-lived provider credential. Give the application under test only the returned `credentials.headers` map. The data plane rejects workspace keys and credentials scoped to another sandbox or environment.
ingress_rules.note: Only in the sense that each environment's apiBaseUrl/mcpUrl endpoint requires a sandbox+environment-scoped, expiring credential; there are no customer ports, IP allowlists or firewall rules.

guest_firewall.quote: Customers are billed for ready environments, not the number of underlying runtime containers.
guest_firewall.note: No customer-accessible machine, shell or root: the API surface is lifecycle + state + provider-shaped REST/MCP only (checked OpenAPI paths).

secret_proxy.quote: Never send a production provider credential to Archal.
secret_proxy.note: No real credentials are involved at all: Archal issues fake, short-lived scoped provider credentials for its simulated services; the TS client 'strips caller-supplied provider authorization and applies the scoped headers from the sandbox connection'. Not a proxy to real APIs.

volume_attach.quote: State persists across provider calls until you load replacement state, reset, or destroy the sandbox. A second sandbox begins from its own declared state and cannot read the first sandbox.
volume_attach.note: No volumes/storage concept; only per-environment JSON/SQL state (max 2 MiB state input).

volume_shared.quote: A sandbox is an isolated runtime containing one or more stateful environments. Its state and credentials do not cross into another sandbox.
volume_shared.note: No shared storage across sandboxes by design; several environments within one sandbox share a lifecycle, not a filesystem.
